messages:
sophie: Quick heads-up. After widening the coalesce window on some hosts, we saw p99s creep up on mixed-traffic runs. I prototyped a small 'grace buffer' that holds very-late arrivals for tiny windows for up to a few dozen ms. Goal: improve pack efficiency without breaking tail latency.

Tom: Clarify: this buffer is per-lane or global per-GPU? How long do items wait and when do they get forced through?

sophie: Per-lane for now. Config sketch: grace_buffer_ms=40, max_buffer_tokens_per_lane=256, eviction_policy=lru_soft, early_drain_threshold_pct=20. If occupancy > threshold or a request has `deadline_ms` <= X, we bypass packing (early drain).

maya: I'm worried about starvation and kvcache pinning. Holding inflight items means we might pin KV entries longer and evict others. Need explicit fairness/eviction rules and an occupancy cap per-tenant.

liam: Agree w/ maya. Also add a memory pressure metric for the kv cache and a hard cap: if kv_pressure > 90% then immediate flush/fallback to normal batching.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: feature flag `sched_grace_buffer`, alpha tenants only, telemetry `buffer_hold_time`, `buffer_evictions`, `kvcache_pressure`, `packing_efficiency`.

Tom: We could accept enqueue hints: `enqueue(req, hint={'deadline_ms':120,'priority':'interactive'})` so scheduler can choose bypass. That keeps API backward compatible.

sophie: Good call. Also fallback: if grace buffer occupancy > 80% for >100ms, trigger canary drain to avoid cascading pileups.

maya: Let's add simulation runs on the replay harness using our tenant mixes, and capture p50/95/99 plus packing efficiency and eviction rates. Build alerts: auto-disable if `buffer_evictions` > 1% or `kvcache_pressure` rises 25% vs baseline.

liam: I'll draft an RFC follow-up with sim results and microbench numbers. Plan: alpha rollout next week to 5 tenants; roll to more if stable. Objections?

maya: none.

sophie: I'll open the feature-flag PR and telemetry tickets. Keep it reversible and tightly instrumented.

Tom: If we see fairness regressions, consider token-rebalance where evicted buffer tokens are recharged to starved tenants. Could be a follow-up.

infra-bot: note: remember to add telemetry tag `experiment=grace_buffer_v1` to all metrics.
